items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: The music that you were playing then, do you think it was similar or has it changed from King Oliver’s and Louis Armstrong’s, early on in jazz.

ctx.x: awfully well in his career, and so I got my start in New Orleans. I call it my apprenticeship in jazz.
The music that you were playing then, do you think it was similar or has it changed from King Oliver’s and Louis Armstrong’s, early on in jazz.

Well I think Dixieland primarily is still the same type of music that it was. It was considered the first type of jazz music. Well first at the turn of the century was I guess what you’d call ragtime music, which was mostly played on the piano. Then the Dixieland bands started out with the Original Dixieland band out of New Orleans, and basically it was played then just about the same as it is now. But there is some influence between other styles of music that have sort of gotten into the simple Dixieland style.…
